subject: Adding control variables to mediation model

messages.author: 1c9a21c1d6060184
messages.subject: Adding control variables to mediation model
parts:
Hi all
I am testing a mediation model in R, here is my model



mediation.modelSem <- '
#dependent variable
Z~Z1+Z2+Z3
#mediating variable
E1=~E11+E12+E13+E14
E2=~E21+E22+E23+E24
E3=~E31+E32+E33+E34
E4=~E41+E42+E43+E44

# independent variable
T1=~T11+T12+T13+T14

T4=~T41+T42+T43+T44
T5=~T51+T52+T53+T54
T6=~T61+T62+T63+T64

#mediating variable
E=~E1+E2+E3+E4
# independent variable
T=~T1+T4+T5+T6
#control variables
P=~P1+Pv2+P3
Tr=~Tr1+Tr2+Tr3
             
# mediator

E ~ a*T

Z~ b*E         

             # direct effect

Z~  c*T+
           # indirect effect (a*b)
ab := a*b

           # total effect
total := c + (a*b)'

I could not figure out how I could add P and Tr as control variables to this model
In addition, I have age and tenure as two other control variables and I do not know how I can add these two to the model.

I appreciate your help. Thank you!

messages.author: f6d12b388faad456
messages.subject: Re: Adding control variables to mediation model
parts:
From what I understood, you can simply write the controller as an IV:

Z~P+Tr

If you want to represent P and Tr as confounders, then you can make them as mediators or as a common cause of both the IV and DV:

Z+T~P+Tr

Hope this helps,
Yago
